The checker tools/provenance/check_provenance.py re-runs every generator and byte-compares its output to the committed file; any difference fails. Both 'path' and 'generator' must be repository-relative (no absolute paths, no '..' components), must stay inside the repository, and must be tracked by git once the repository has commits. Generators are executed through tools/provenance/guard_runner.py, which installs a Python audit hook before the generator code runs; the hook refuses imports of network, process, and native-capability modules and blocks the known socket, process-creation, and native-call audit events. That runner is a best-effort in-process guard, not a sandbox or a confinement mechanism: repository source review of every generator script and the CI checks are the operative controls (CI is the authoritative automated verification; from Phase 3's visibility flip the branch ruleset makes it a mechanically enforced merge requirement - see SECURITY.md's activation record). JSON is treated as a data format: a tracked .json file is allowed only if it is one of the checker's known configuration files (KNOWN_CONFIG_JSON in the checker) or listed here. Committed fixtures must be tiny; the cap is the checker's own MAX_FIXTURE_BYTES, which carries the record of what it was raised from and why.
